cases.prompt: In this Astro project, turn the Markdown files in src/data/blog into a blog. Define a content collection for them with a schema for title, pubDate and an optional draft flag, and add a page at /blog/<post id>/ that renders each post that is not a draft.
cases.expected_output: A content collection named for the blog posts is defined with a loader and a schema, and a dynamic route under src/pages/blog renders each non-draft post. The project builds with Astro 7.
assertions: The collection is defined in `src/content.config.ts` with a `loader` that reads `src/data/blog`.
The schema validates title, pubDate and an optional draft field.
The blog route renders post bodies with the `render()` function from `astro:content`.
Draft posts do not get a page.

cases.prompt: This Astro project was written for Astro 4. The astro dependency in package.json has just been bumped to Astro 7 and the site no longer builds. Update the code so it builds on Astro 7. Keep the same pages and URLs.
cases.expected_output: The project builds on Astro 7 with the home page and one page per blog post at the same URLs as before. Removed Astro APIs are replaced with their current equivalents.
assertions: The content collection config is at `src/content.config.ts` and the blog collection has a `loader`.
No code uses `Astro.glob`, `entry.render()`, `entry.slug`, `<ViewTransitions />` or `output: 'hybrid'`.
The unclosed `<h1>` in the blog post page is closed.
Blog posts are still served at /blog/hello-world/ and /blog/second-post/.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, add an endpoint at /api/time.json that returns the current server time as JSON, computed on every request. Every other page must stay statically generated. The site will be deployed as a standalone Node server.
cases.expected_output: A /api/time.json endpoint renders on demand and returns the current time as JSON, the Node adapter is configured, and the existing pages are still prerendered.
assertions: The endpoint is rendered on demand, not prerendered at build time.
The existing pages remain prerendered.
An adapter for Node is installed and set in the Astro config.
The config does not use `output: 'hybrid'`.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, add the remark-toc plugin so that the `## Contents` heading in src/pages/guide.md is followed by a generated table of contents in the built page.
cases.expected_output: remark-toc is installed and registered so that the built guide page contains a generated list of links under the Contents heading.
assertions: `remark-toc` is added to the project's dependencies.
`@astrojs/markdown-remark` is added to the project's dependencies, because Astro 7 no longer includes the remark pipeline by default.
The Astro config registers remark-toc through a Markdown processor configuration that runs remark plugins.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, add a newsletter sign-up form to the home page. Implement the submission as an Astro action that validates the email address and returns a success message. The form must work without client-side JavaScript. The site will be deployed as a standalone Node server.
cases.expected_output: An action validates the submitted email, the home page has a form that posts to it and shows the result, and the project is configured to render that page on demand with the Node adapter.
assertions: The action is exported from the `server` object in `src/actions/index.ts` and accepts form data.
The email is validated with a schema that uses `z` imported from `astro/zod`.
The home page form uses `method="POST"` with the action as its `action` attribute and reads the result on the server.
The home page is rendered on demand and an adapter is configured.

cases.prompt: Add Tailwind CSS to this Astro project and use utility classes to make the home page heading large and bold.
cases.expected_output: Tailwind CSS 4 is set up through its Vite plugin with a global stylesheet imported by the layout, and the home page heading uses Tailwind utility classes.
assertions: Tailwind is added through `@tailwindcss/vite` in the Vite plugins of the Astro config.
The legacy `@astrojs/tailwind` integration is not used.
A stylesheet contains `@import "tailwindcss"` and is imported so it applies to the home page.
The home page heading has utility classes for size and weight.

cases.prompt: Enable Astro's client-side router with animated page transitions for every page of this Astro project.
cases.expected_output: The shared layout enables Astro's client router so navigation between pages is animated.
assertions: The shared layout renders `<ClientRouter />` imported from `astro:transitions` inside `<head>`.
The removed `<ViewTransitions />` component is not used.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, the home page should show a site announcement read from an ANNOUNCEMENT environment variable, and server code will need an API_SECRET variable. Declare both with Astro's built-in type-safe environment variable support so they are validated, with ANNOUNCEMENT optional and public and API_SECRET kept out of client bundles, and show the announcement on the home page when it is set.
cases.expected_output: Both variables are declared in an env schema in the Astro config, the home page reads ANNOUNCEMENT through Astro's typed env module and renders it when set, and API_SECRET is declared as a server-only secret.
assertions: The Astro config declares `env.schema` with `envField` entries for ANNOUNCEMENT and API_SECRET.
API_SECRET is declared with server context and secret access.
The home page imports ANNOUNCEMENT from an `astro:env` module rather than reading `process.env`.
The announcement is only rendered when the variable is set.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, extend the PostHeader component to show a byline under the title that reads like "By Ada Lovelace on 10 December 1815", with the author name in bold and the date in a <time> element that has a machine-readable datetime attribute.
cases.expected_output: The built home page shows the byline with a space on each side of the bold author name and before the date, and the date is in a <time> element with a datetime attribute.
assertions: The rendered byline reads "By Ada Lovelace on 10 December 1815" with spaces between the words and the inline elements.
The author name is in a `<strong>` element and the date in a `<time datetime=...>` element.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, show a paragraph with the text "This site is in beta." at the top of the home page, but only when the PUBLIC_SHOW_BETA environment variable is set to true. The .env file currently sets it to false.
cases.expected_output: The home page renders the beta notice only when PUBLIC_SHOW_BETA is the string "true". With the current .env value of false, the built page does not contain the notice.
assertions: The condition treats the variable as a string or declares it as a boolean with `astro:env`; it does not rely on the truthiness of `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_SHOW_BETA`.
With PUBLIC_SHOW_BETA=false the built home page does not contain the notice.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, add the image at src/assets/hero.png to the top of the home page, above the post header, with the alt text "Abstract purple banner".
cases.expected_output: The built home page has an with the alt text whose src points at a processed asset under /_astro/, and that asset exists in the build output.
assertions: The image is imported from `src/assets/` and rendered with `` from `astro:assets` or an `` using the import's `src`.
The built page does not reference `/src/assets/hero.png`.
The image has the requested alt text.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, the Menu button in the header opens the navigation on the first page load, but stops working after following a link to another page. Fix it without removing the page transitions.
cases.expected_output: The menu toggle is set up again after each client-side navigation, and the client router is still enabled.
assertions: The toggle setup runs on the `astro:page-load` event, or uses another approach that survives client-side navigation such as a delegated listener on `document`.
`<ClientRouter />` is still rendered in the layout.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, the product pages at /products/[id] are rendered on demand. Cache their responses for 10 minutes, keep serving a stale response for up to 1 more minute while it is refreshed, and tag them "products" so they can be invalidated together. Use Astro's built-in route caching with the in-memory provider.
cases.expected_output: Route caching is enabled with the in-memory provider at the top level of the Astro config, and product pages are cached for 600 seconds with 60 seconds of stale-while-revalidate and the tag products. The project builds.
assertions: The Astro config sets `cache: { provider: memoryCache() }` at the top level, not under `experimental`.
Product pages are cached with `maxAge: 600`, `swr: 60` and the tag `products`, through `Astro.cache.set()` in the page or `routeRules` in the config.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, add a page at /visits that shows how many times the current visitor has loaded it. Keep the count in server-side session storage, not in a cookie value or in the browser.
cases.expected_output: A /visits page rendered on demand reads the visitor's count from the Astro session, increments it, stores it and displays it. The project builds.
assertions: The page is rendered on demand.
The count is read with an awaited `Astro.session.get()` and stored with `Astro.session.set()`.
No session driver is configured by hand; the Node adapter provides one.

cases.prompt: In this Astro project, add the Counter component from src/components/Counter.jsx to the home page, below the paragraph, so visitors can use it.
cases.expected_output: The home page renders the Counter component as a hydrated island, so its buttons work in the browser.
assertions: The Counter is rendered with a `client:*` directive.
The built home page contains an island for the component.

cases.prompt: Count how many times each word appears in word-list.txt and write the counts to counts.txt, one "word count" pair per line, sorted from most to least frequent.
cases.expected_output: counts.txt lists apple 3, banana 2 and cherry 1, in that order.
assertions: counts.txt reports apple 3, banana 2, cherry 1.
The counts are listed from most to least frequent.

cases.prompt: In this Vite and React project, add a Counter component with increment and decrement buttons and render it in App.
cases.expected_output: A Counter React component with working increment and decrement buttons exists and App renders it. The project remains a plain Vite and React app.
assertions: A Counter component keeps its count in React state and has increment and decrement buttons.
App renders the Counter component.
No Astro dependency or configuration is added to the project.
